title: Automation Tricks
intro: Automation is what separates a static mix from a moving one. Logic has two kinds: track automation stays tied to its place on the timeline, while region automation travels with its region. Knowing which one you are in explains most automation surprises.

tips.t: Use Region automation for anything that belongs to the part
tips.d: A filter sweep that is part of a synth riff should move with the riff. Region automation does that; track automation does not.

src.label: Apple — Track automation vs region automation in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Press A to toggle automation view
tips.d: Press A to show or hide track automation. In the Audio Track Editor it does the same job as the Show/Hide Automation button.

tips.t: Use Latch mode for almost everything
tips.d: Latch writes while you move the control and holds the last value when you let go. Touch snaps back, Write erases as it goes, and Read plays only. Latch is the right default.

src.label: Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Never leave a track in Write mode
tips.d: Write mode erases existing automation as the playhead passes, whether you touch the fader or not.

src.label: Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Delete an automation point without dragging it
tips.d: Double-click the point, or select it and press Delete, or drag across it with the Eraser.

src.label: Apple — Delete automation in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Hold ⌃⇧ and, with the Pointer tool, drag the line between two automation points to bend it into a curve. This works as long as the two points aren't directly above each other.

tips.t: Trim existing automation up or down
tips.d: Trim is not a mode on its own. It works in combination with Touch or Latch. With it on, moving the fader offsets existing automation up or down by the amount you move it. It applies only to Volume, Pan and Send levels, so use it to lift an already-automated vocal without redrawing its moves.

src.label: Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Relative mode to layer a second pass
tips.d: Relative automation sits on top of your existing pass as an offset, so you can add a ride without destroying the original moves.

src.label: Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Marquee a range, then drag the line to change only that section
tips.d: Drag across the bars you want to change with the Marquee tool, then drag the automation line inside that selection. Logic creates two automation points at the left edge and two at the right edge of the selection, so the change stays boxed in and does not bleed into the surrounding bars.

src.label: Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Show several automation lanes at once
tips.d: Instead of switching one automation curve between parameters, show automation sub-lanes, which appear below the main track. Click the automation sub-lane disclosure triangle, then choose each lane's parameter from its Automation Parameter pop-up menu. You can then see several parameters at once.

tips.t: Delete all automation on a track in one command
tips.d: Choose Mix > Delete Automation > Delete All Automation on Selected Track to remove every automation parameter from that track at once. The same submenu has Delete Visible Automation on Selected Track, which removes only the active parameter, and Delete Orphaned Automation on Selected Track. Automation can become orphaned when it is copied between tracks.

src.label: Apple — Delete automation in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Thin dense automation after recording a controller pass
tips.d: Delete Redundant Automation Points cleans up heavy controller passes, but it is global: it removes redundant points on all regions and all tracks, not just your selection. To thin one passage only, select the points in that range and press Delete, then redraw.

src.label: Apple — Delete automation in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Snap automation to the grid when it needs to be rhythmic
tips.d: Open the Snap pop-up menu in the Tracks area, choose Snap Automation, and pick a value from the submenu. Automation edits then snap to that value, so filter stabs land on the grid. You can set it independently in the Tracks area and the Piano Roll Editor.
